data.title: Kyoto & Osaka, Japan: 7 Days of Temples, Food & Culture
data.subtitle: Ancient shrines, geisha districts, street food and a night in a traditional ryokan

activities.title: Arrive at KIX and ride the Haruka Express to Kyoto
activities.description: Land at Kansai International. Buy an ICOCA card, then take the Haruka Express (about 75 min, ~3,000 JPY) to Kyoto Station. Check in at Hotel Gracery Kyoto Sanjo (mid-range), The Millennials Kyoto (capsule-style, modern) or K's House Kyoto (budget hostel).

activities.title: Dinner in Pontocho Alley
activities.description: Narrow lantern-lit alley parallel to the Kamo River. Try yakitori, obanzai (Kyoto home cooking) or a riverside terrace in summer. Book ahead on weekends.

activities.title: Evening stroll along the Kamo River
activities.description: Easy walk to settle in. Locals sit along the river steps at night; grab a drink from a konbini and relax.

activities.title: Fushimi Inari Taisha at sunrise
activities.description: Thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up Mt. Inari. Free, open 24 hours. Go before 7am for empty gates and soft light. Allow 2-3 hours for the full summit hike (about 230 m climb) or turn back at Yotsutsuji for the best view.

activities.title: Kiyomizu-dera and Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka
activities.description: UNESCO-listed wooden temple on a hillside with a huge stage and city views (400 JPY). Walk down the preserved lanes of Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka for sweets, pottery and matcha ice cream.

activities.title: Yasaka Shrine and Maruyama Park
activities.description: Walk north through Higashiyama to Yasaka Shrine and the park beside it. Lunch nearby on udon or soba.

activities.title: Gion at dusk
activities.description: Walk Hanami-koji and Shirakawa canal to spot geiko and maiko heading to appointments. Be respectful: no chasing or blocking, no photos in private alleys.

activities.title: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
activities.description: Zen temple covered in gold leaf, reflected in a mirror pond. Entry 500 JPY. Arrive at opening to avoid tour groups. Allow 45 min.

activities.title: Ryoan-ji rock garden
activities.description: Famous dry-stone Zen garden with 15 rocks. Sit on the veranda and soak up the quiet. About 30 min walk or 10 min by bus from Kinkaku-ji.

activities.title: Lunch at Nishiki Market
activities.description: Kyoto's Kitchen: five blocks of stalls selling pickles, tamagoyaki, tofu donuts, grilled seafood and sake tastings. Eat as you walk.

activities.title: Tea ceremony experience
activities.description: Book a small-group matcha ceremony in Gion (about 3,000-5,000 JPY). Learn the etiquette and enjoy wagashi sweets. Reserve 1-2 months ahead in peak season.

activities.title: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
activities.description: Towering bamboo path in western Kyoto. Arrive before 8am for quiet and golden light. Take the JR Sagano line from Kyoto Station (15 min).

activities.title: Tenryu-ji Temple and gardens
activities.description: UNESCO Zen temple with a pond garden designed in the 14th century. Exit through the north gate straight into the bamboo grove.

activities.title: Iwatayama Monkey Park and Togetsukyo Bridge
activities.description: 20 minute uphill walk to a hilltop with free-roaming macaques and sweeping views over Kyoto. Then stroll across Togetsukyo Bridge and have tofu or soba lunch by the river.

activities.title: Check in to a ryokan with onsen and kaiseki
activities.description: Splurge night: a traditional ryokan in Arashiyama (e.g. Hoshinoya Kyoto, accessible only by boat) or a Gion ryokan. Soak in the onsen, wear a yukata and enjoy a multi-course kaiseki dinner. Book 1-2 months ahead.

activities.title: Train to Nara
activities.description: Kintetsu Nara Line or JR Nara Line from Kyoto, about 45 min.

activities.title: Todai-ji and the Great Buddha
activities.description: World's largest bronze Buddha inside one of the largest wooden buildings. Entry 800 JPY.

activities.title: Nara Park deer and lunch
activities.description: Feed the sacred deer with shika-senbei crackers (200 JPY). Bow and they bow back. Lunch on kakinoha-zushi (persimmon-leaf sushi).

activities.title: Kasuga Taisha lantern path then back to Kyoto
activities.description: Walk through a forest of thousands of stone and bronze lanterns. Return to Kyoto by evening and pack for Osaka.

activities.title: Shinkansen/JR Special Rapid to Osaka and hotel drop
activities.description: About 30 min from Kyoto Station to Osaka. Drop bags at Cross Hotel Osaka (Dotonbori) or Hotel Hankyu Respire (Umeda).

activities.title: Osaka Castle and park
activities.description: Reconstructed 16th century castle with an 8th-floor observation deck and great museum. Grounds are beautiful at cherry blossom time.

activities.title: Dotonbori food crawl
activities.description: Neon-lit canalside street. Takoyaki (Wanaka, Creo-Ru), okonomiyaki (Mizuno), kushikatsu, gyoza and ramen. Photo at the Glico Running Man sign.

activities.title: Kuromon Market breakfast
activities.description: Osaka's Kitchen: fresh sushi, grilled scallops, fugu, wagyu skewers and strawberry mochi.

activities.title: Shinsekai and Tsutenkaku Tower
activities.description: Retro neighbourhood with kushikatsu restaurants and the Tsutenkaku Tower. Try the fried-skewer rules: no double dipping!

activities.title: Umeda Sky Building Floating Garden Observatory
activities.description: 360-degree views from the rooftop observatory (1,500 JPY). Head to KIX by the Haruka or Nankai line afterwards (allow 90 min before international flights).

data.description:
A 7-day first-timer's loop through Japan's Kansai region. Base yourself in Kyoto for temples, gardens and tea houses, then finish in Osaka for nightlife and street food. Best seasons: late March to April (cherry blossoms) and mid-November (autumn leaves). Budget roughly $150-250 USD per person per day.

GETTING THERE & AROUND: Fly into Kansai International (KIX). The Haruka Express takes about 75 min to Kyoto Station. Buy an ICOCA card for trains, buses and konbini. Kyoto buses get crowded, so the subway and walking work best.

WHERE TO STAY
- Kyoto (nights 1-5): Hotel Gracery Kyoto Sanjo or The Millennials Kyoto for mid-range; Hoshinoya Kyoto for luxury; K's House Kyoto for budget hostel beds.
- Ryokan splurge (night 4): Book a traditional ryokan in Arashiyama or Gion with kaiseki dinner and an onsen bath.
- Osaka (nights 6-7): Cross Hotel Osaka in Dotonbori or Hotel Hankyu Respire for easy station access.

DAY BY DAY
Day 1: Arrive, check in, evening stroll along Kamo River and dinner in Pontocho Alley.
Day 2: Fushimi Inari Shrine at sunrise (thousands of red torii gates), then Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka streets, and Gion at dusk to spot geisha.
Day 3: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion), Ryoan-ji rock garden, then Nishiki Market for lunch. Evening tea ceremony.
Day 4: Arashiyama bamboo grove, Tenryu-ji, Iwatayama monkey park, Togetsukyo Bridge. Overnight at the ryokan.
Day 5: Day trip to Nara: Todai-ji with its giant Buddha, and the friendly deer in Nara Park (about 45 min by train).
Day 6: Move to Osaka. Osaka Castle, then Dotonbori at night: takoyaki, okonomiyaki, kushikatsu.
Day 7: Kuromon Market breakfast, Shinsekai district, Umeda Sky Building views, then head to the airport.

MUST-EATS: Kaiseki dinner, Nishiki Market skewers, matcha everything in Uji, takoyaki and okonomiyaki in Osaka, kushikatsu in Shinsekai.

TIPS: Visit Fushimi Inari before 7am to beat crowds. Carry cash for small shops and shrines. Be quiet and respectful in Gion's private alleys. Book ryokan and any tea ceremony 1-2 months ahead in peak season.

data.title: Cusco, Sacred Valley & Machu Picchu, Peru: 7 Days in the Andes
data.subtitle: Inca ruins, colourful markets, the Sacred Valley and a sunrise at Machu Picchu

activities.title: Arrive in Lima (LIM) and check in
activities.description: Jorge Chavez International Airport, Av. Elmer Faucett s/n, Callao 07031. Take a pre-booked taxi to Miraflores (45-60 min in traffic). Stay at Belmond Miraflores Park (Av. Malecon de la Reserva 1035, Miraflores), Hotel B (Jiron Saenz Pena 204, Barranco) or a hostel near Parque Kennedy.

activities.title: Malecon de Miraflores clifftop walk
activities.description: Paved clifftop path above the Pacific with parks, paragliders and the Parque del Amor. Address: Malecon de la Reserva, Miraflores 15074.

activities.title: Huaca Pucllana at sunset
activities.description: Adobe pyramid from about 500 AD in the middle of Miraflores. Address: Calle General Borgoño cuadra 8, Miraflores 15074.

activities.title: Ceviche dinner
activities.description: Try classic leche de tigre and ceviche at La Mar Cebicheria (Av. Mariscal La Mar 770, Miraflores) or splurge on the tasting menu at Central (Av. Pedro de Osma 301, Barranco), booked months ahead.

activities.title: Fly Lima to Cusco
activities.description: LATAM or Sky Airline, about 1 hr 30 min. Land at Alejandro Velasco Astete Airport, Av. Velasco Astete s/n, Cusco 08000. Drink coca tea at the hotel and take it slow.

activities.title: Check in and rest to acclimatize
activities.description: Stay at Belmond Hotel Monasterio (Calle Palacios 136, Cusco 08002), Tierra Viva Cusco Plaza (Suecia 345, Cusco 08002) or a hostel in San Blas.

activities.title: Plaza de Armas and Cathedral
activities.description: The old Inca heart of the city, ringed by colonial arcades. Visit the Cathedral (Plaza de Armas s/n, Cusco 08002) and La Compañia de Jesus church next door.

activities.title: Coffee at MAP Cafe or Cicciolina
activities.description: Light snacks only on the first day. MAP Cafe: Plaza Nazarenas 231, Cusco 08002. Cicciolina: Calle Triunfo 393, 2nd floor, Cusco 08002.

activities.title: San Pedro Market
activities.description: Local market for fruit juices, cheese, textiles and breakfast. Address: Calle Cascaparo s/n, Cusco 08002.

activities.title: Qorikancha (Temple of the Sun)
activities.description: Inca temple foundations under the Santo Domingo convent (entry about 15 PEN). Address: Plazoleta Santo Domingo s/n, Cusco 08002.

activities.title: Lunch at Chicha by Gaston Acurio
activities.description: Modern Andean cooking: alpaca, cuy and ceviche. Address: Plaza Regocijo 261, Cusco 08002.

activities.title: Saqsaywaman fortress
activities.description: Massive Inca fortress above the city with 100-ton stones fitted perfectly. Entry is part of the Boleto Turistico (about 130 PEN, 10 days). Address: Saqsaywaman Archaeological Park, Cusco 08002.

activities.title: Pisco sour tasting at Museo del Pisco
activities.description: Learn to make a pisco sour with food pairings. Address: Calle Santa Catalina Ancha 398, Cusco 08002.

activities.title: Transfer to Pisac (about 1 hr)
activities.description: Hire a driver or take a colectivo from Calle Puputi in Cusco. Address of Pisac main square: Plaza de Armas, Pisac 08170.

activities.title: Pisac Inca ruins and market
activities.description: Hilltop terraces and ceremonial areas above the village (entry via Boleto Turistico). Then browse the artisan market in the main square. Address: Pisac Archaeological Park, Pisac 08170.

activities.title: Maras salt mines
activities.description: Thousands of white salt pans cascading down a mountainside, in use since Inca times (entry about 20 PEN). Address: Salineras de Maras, Maras 08720.

activities.title: Moray terraces
activities.description: Circular Inca agricultural terraces used as a laboratory for crops. Address: Moray Archaeological Site, Maras 08720.

activities.title: Check in to a Sacred Valley stay
activities.description: Sleep low: stay at Inkaterra Hacienda Urubamba (Carretera Urubamba-Ollantaytambo, Urubamba), a boutique stay in Urubamba, or a guesthouse in Ollantaytambo.

activities.title: Ollantaytambo fortress
activities.description: Inca fortress and temple terraces towering over a living Inca town (Boleto Turistico). Address: Ollantaytambo Archaeological Park, Ollantaytambo 08660.

activities.title: Lunch in Ollantaytambo
activities.description: Cobbled streets lined with cafes. Try Heart's Cafe (Calle Principal, Ollantaytambo) for fresh Andean food.

activities.title: Train to Aguas Calientes
activities.location: Andenes Del Inca Hotel at Ollantaytambo | Train Station | Sacred Valley
activities.description: PeruRail or Inca Rail (about 1.5 hours, about 60-100 USD one-way). Depart Ollantaytambo Station, Av. Ferrocarril s/n, Ollantaytambo 08660.

activities.title: Check in and rest, early night
activities.description: Aguas Calientes (Machu Picchu Pueblo). Stay at Inkaterra Machu Picchu Pueblo Hotel (Prolongacion Imperio de los Incas, Aguas Calientes) or a mid-range hotel near the station. Eat early and sleep early: the first bus leaves at 5:30 AM.

activities.title: Bus up to Machu Picchu
activities.description: Consettur shuttle bus from Av. Hermanos Ayar, Aguas Calientes 08680 (about 25 min, about 12 USD return). Line up early; carry your passport and ticket.

activities.title: Machu Picchu circuit
activities.description: UNESCO Wonder of the World. Walk the main circuit with a guide: Temple of the Sun, Intihuatana stone, Sacred Plaza and the classic postcard viewpoint. Allow 3-4 hours. Address: Machu Picchu Historic Sanctuary, Machu Picchu 08680.

activities.title: Optional hike: Huayna Picchu or Machu Picchu Mountain
activities.description: Extra permit required: book far in advance. Steep, narrow stairs with a dramatic view. Address: Huayna Picchu Trailhead, Machu Picchu 08680.

activities.title: Train back towards Cusco
activities.description: Return via Ollantaytambo and a connecting bus or car to Cusco (about 3.5-4 hours in total). Aguas Calientes Station: Av. Imperio de los Incas, Aguas Calientes 08680.

activities.title: San Blas neighbourhood stroll
activities.description: Artsy hillside quarter of cobbled lanes, workshops and cafes. Address: Plazoleta San Blas, Cusco 08002.

activities.title: Last coffee and souvenirs
activities.description: Browse alpaca textiles and ceramics at Centro Artesanal Cusco (Av. El Sol, Cusco 08002) and buy single-origin Peruvian coffee at a San Blas cafe.

activities.title: Fly out of Cusco
activities.description: Head to Alejandro Velasco Astete International Airport (Av. Velasco Astete s/n, Cusco 08000). Allow 2 hours before domestic and 3 before international flights.

data.description:
A 7-day Peru classic: a day in Lima's food scene, then up into the Andes for Cusco's Inca stonework, the Sacred Valley's markets and terraces, and Machu Picchu itself. Best months: May to September (dry season; June to August is busiest, so book early). Budget roughly $90-250 USD per person per day.

ALTITUDE WARNING: Cusco sits at about 3,400 m (11,150 ft). Take it slow on arrival, drink coca tea, avoid heavy meals and alcohol the first night, and talk to a doctor about altitude sickness. The Sacred Valley is lower (about 2,800 m), which is why many people sleep there first.

GETTING THERE & AROUND: Fly into Lima (LIM), then a 1.5 hr domestic flight to Cusco (CUZ). In the Sacred Valley use taxis, colectivos or a private driver. Machu Picchu: PeruRail or Inca Rail from Ollantaytambo to Aguas Calientes (about 1.5 hrs), then a shuttle bus up. Entry tickets to Machu Picchu are timed and limited: buy them on the official Ministry of Culture site months ahead, and get your circuit and time slot confirmed. Carry your passport for tickets and trains.

WHERE TO STAY
- Lima (night 1): Miraflores is best: Belmond Miraflores Park (luxury, Av. Malecon de la Reserva 1035), Hotel B (boutique, Domeyer 301, Barranco) or a hostel near Parque Kennedy.
- Cusco (nights 2-3 and 7): Belmond Hotel Monasterio (luxury in a 16th-century monastery, Calle Palacios 136), Tierra Viva Cusco Plaza (mid-range, Suecia 345), or a hostel in San Blas for budget.
- Sacred Valley (night 4): Inkaterra Hacienda Urubamba (luxury), a boutique stay in Urubamba or a simple guesthouse in Ollantaytambo.
- Aguas Calientes (night 5): Inkaterra Machu Picchu Pueblo Hotel (luxury), or a mid-range hotel near the train station.

DAY BY DAY
Day 1: Arrive in Lima, Miraflores clifftop walk and a ceviche dinner.
Day 2: Fly to Cusco, take it easy, wander the Plaza de Armas and eat early.
Day 3: Cusco sights: Qorikancha, San Pedro Market, Saqsaywaman and a pisco sour.
Day 4: Sacred Valley: Pisac market and ruins, Maras salt mines and Moray terraces.
Day 5: Ollantaytambo fortress, then train to Aguas Calientes.
Day 6: Machu Picchu at opening, then train back to Cusco.
Day 7: San Blas and last Cusco coffee, then depart.

MUST-EATS: Ceviche in Lima, lomo saltado, cuy (guinea pig) if you are brave, alpaca steak, quinoa soup, ají de gallina, pisco sour and chicha morada.

TIPS: Book Machu Picchu tickets and trains months ahead. Bring cash (soles) for markets and small shops. Carry sunscreen, rain jacket and layers: weather swings between sun and cold rain. Only use official taxis and avoid unlicensed buses. Respect the sites: no climbing on walls, no drones.

data.title: Bali, Indonesia: 7 Days of Temples, Rice Terraces & Beaches
data.subtitle: Ubud jungle, sacred water temples, Tanah Lot at sunset, Uluwatu cliffs and a day trip to Nusa Penida

activities.title: Arrive in Bali and transfer to Ubud
activities.location: I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport
activities.description: Ngurah Rai International Airport, Jl. Raya Gusti Ngurah Rai, Tuban, Kuta, Badung 80362. Pre-book a driver or Grab (about 1.5 hrs to Ubud). Stay at Komaneka at Bisma (Jl. Bisma, Ubud), Alaya Resort Ubud (Jl. Hanoman, Ubud) or a Penestanan homestay.

activities.title: Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary
activities.description: Forest of ancient temples and about 1,000 long-tailed macaques (entry about 100,000 IDR). Keep food and sunglasses hidden. Address: Jl. Monkey Forest, Ubud, Gianyar 80571.

activities.title: Ubud Palace and Ubud Market
activities.description: Royal palace complex and the central market for souvenirs and sarongs. Address: Jl. Raya Ubud No.8, Ubud, Gianyar 80571.

activities.title: Legong dance performance
activities.description: Nightly traditional dance in a temple setting (about 100,000-150,000 IDR). Performances often at Ubud Palace, Jl. Raya Ubud No.8, Ubud 80571.

activities.title: Sunrise at Tegalalang Rice Terraces
activities.description: Layered green terraces north of Ubud (small donation entry). Go early for empty paths and soft light. Address: Tegallalang, Gianyar 80561.

activities.title: Tirta Empul holy water temple
activities.description: Join locals in the purification ritual in the spring pools (rent a sarong; entry about 50,000 IDR). Address: Jl. Tirta, Manukaya, Tampaksiring, Gianyar 80552.

activities.title: Lunch at Ibu Oka
activities.description: Famous babi guling (suckling pig), served with crackling and rice. Address: Jl. Tegal Sari No.2, Ubud, Gianyar 80571.

activities.title: Campuhan Ridge Walk at golden hour
activities.description: Easy 2 km grassy ridge path between two valleys, best late afternoon. Address: Jl. Raya Campuhan, Ubud, Gianyar 80571.

activities.title: Balinese cooking class
activities.description: Market visit and hands-on cooking of satay, sambal and curries at Paon Bali Cooking Class (Laplapan, Ubud, Gianyar). Book 1-2 days ahead (about 350,000-450,000 IDR).

activities.title: Ubud Art Market
activities.description: Bargain for handwoven baskets, batik and carvings. Address: Jl. Raya Ubud No.35, Ubud, Gianyar 80571.

activities.title: Saraswati Temple and Lotus Pond
activities.description: Beautiful lotus-pond temple. Address: Jl. Raya Ubud, Ubud, Gianyar 80571.

activities.title: Sunset dinner at a rice-field cafe
activities.description: Try Sayan House or Sari Organik (Jl. Subak Sok Wayah, Ubud) for organic food with terrace views.

activities.title: Drive from Ubud toward Tanah Lot
activities.description: About 1.5 to 2 hours with a private driver (about 600,000-800,000 IDR for the day).

activities.title: Beraban Village and Tanah Lot area
activities.description: Stroll the cliff paths and shops before the temple fills up. Address: Beraban, Kediri, Tabanan 82121.

activities.title: Tanah Lot sunset
activities.description: Sea temple on a rocky outcrop at high tide (entry about 60,000 IDR). Arrive 90 minutes before sunset. Address: Beraban, Kediri, Tabanan, Bali 82121.

activities.title: Check in at Uluwatu
activities.description: Stay at Alila Villas Uluwatu (Jl. Belimbing Sari, Banjar Tambiyak, Pecatu), Suarga Padang Padang (Jl. Labuansait, Pecatu) or a homestay near Bingin.

activities.title: Padang Padang Beach
activities.description: Small beach in a limestone cove (famous from Eat Pray Love). Entry about 10,000 IDR. Address: Pecatu, South Kuta, Badung 80361.

activities.title: Bingin Beach and lunch
activities.description: Steep stairs down to surfers' beach and cliffside warungs. Address: Jl. Pantai Bingin, Pecatu, South Kuta, Badung 80361.

activities.title: Uluwatu Temple at sunset
activities.description: Clifftop sea temple 70 m above the Indian Ocean (entry about 50,000 IDR). Beware of monkeys stealing glasses and phones. Address: Pecatu, South Kuta, Badung 80361.

activities.title: Kecak fire dance
activities.description: Nightly show in the cliffside amphitheatre next to the temple, with 70 chanting performers (about 150,000 IDR). Address: Uluwatu Temple Amphitheater, Pecatu 80361.

activities.title: Fast boat from Sanur to Nusa Penida
activities.description: Booking with a day tour or operator. Departs Sanur Beach harbour, Jl. Hang Tuah, Sanur, Denpasar 80228 (about 45 min crossing).

activities.title: Kelingking Beach viewpoint
activities.description: The famous T-Rex-shaped cliff and beach. The path down is extremely steep and risky: the viewpoint is enough. Address: Bunga Mekar, Nusa Penida, Klungkung 80771.

activities.title: Angel's Billabong and Broken Beach
activities.description: Natural rock pool and a sea-carved arch. Stay back from the edge: waves can be dangerous. Address: Ped, Nusa Penida, Klungkung 80771.

activities.title: Return to mainland
activities.description: Fast boat back to Sanur and car to Uluwatu (about 1 hr 15 min).

activities.title: Beach breakfast at Jimbaran Bay
activities.description: Calm bay and a long sandy beach lined with seafood restaurants (Menega Cafe, Jl. Four Seasons, Jimbaran). Try grilled snapper or prawns.

activities.title: Last swim and souvenirs
activities.description: Buy coffee, spices and batik at the Jimbaran Fish Market or Sukawati art market. Address: Jimbaran, South Kuta, Badung 80361.

activities.title: Head to the airport
activities.location: I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport
activities.description: Ngurah Rai International Airport, Jl. Raya Gusti Ngurah Rai, Tuban, Kuta, Badung 80362. About 20 min from Jimbaran. Arrive 3 hours before international flights.

data.description:
A 7-day Bali loop: three days in Ubud's rice terraces, temples and cooking classes, a sunset at Tanah Lot, two days on the Uluwatu clifftops and beaches, and a boat day to Nusa Penida's dramatic coastline. Best months: April to October (dry season). Budget roughly $60-200 USD per person per day.

GETTING THERE & AROUND: Fly into Ngurah Rai International (DPS). Hire a private driver for the day (about 600,000-800,000 IDR, 8-10 hrs) or use Grab/Gojek ride-hailing: both work in most tourist areas. Renting a scooter is common but risky: you need an international licence with a motorbike endorsement and insurance. Traffic is heavy around Canggu and Seminyak, so add buffer time.

WHERE TO STAY
- Ubud (nights 1-3): Komaneka at Bisma (luxury, Jl. Bisma, Ubud), Alaya Resort Ubud (mid-range, Jl. Hanoman), or a homestay in Penestanan or Nyuh Kuning (budget, about 20-30 USD).
- Uluwatu (nights 4-6): Alila Villas Uluwatu or Bulgari Resort (luxury cliff-edge), Suarga Padang Padang (mid-range), or homestays and hostels near Bingin and Padang Padang beach.
- Night 7: Jimbaran or near the airport (for an early flight).

DAY BY DAY
Day 1: Arrive, transfer to Ubud, Sacred Monkey Forest and Ubud Palace, evening Legong dance.
Day 2: Sunrise at Tegalalang Rice Terraces, Tirta Empul water temple, Campuhan Ridge Walk at golden hour.
Day 3: Balinese cooking class, Ubud Art Market, Saraswati Temple and sunset at a rice-field cafe.
Day 4: Drive to Tanah Lot for sunset, then on to Uluwatu.
Day 5: Padang Padang and Bingin beaches, Uluwatu Temple at sunset and Kecak fire dance.
Day 6: Boat to Nusa Penida: Kelingking Beach, Angel's Billabong, Broken Beach.
Day 7: Jimbaran Bay beach breakfast, last swim and depart.

MUST-EATS: Babi guling (suckling pig) at Ibu Oka in Ubud, nasi campur, satay lilit, mie goreng, fresh coconuts, smoothie bowls, grilled seafood on Jimbaran Bay.

TIPS: Wear a sarong and sash at temples (rent or buy at the entrance). Respect offerings on the ground: do not step on them. Drink only bottled or filtered water. Bring cash (IDR) for small warungs and temples. Book Nusa Penida fast boats early in the morning and check sea conditions: crossings can be rough.

data.title: Lisbon, Sintra & Porto, Portugal: 7 Days of Tiles, Palaces & Port Wine
data.subtitle: Pastel de nata, fairytale palaces, tram rides and a day in the Douro Valley vineyards

activities.title: Arrive in Lisbon and check in
activities.description: Fly into Lisbon (LIS) and take the red metro line to the centre (about 20 min). Stay at Memmo Alfama (luxury boutique, rooftop pool), Lisboa Carmo Hotel (mid-range, Chiado) or Home Lisbon Hostel (budget, social dinners).

activities.title: Wander Alfama's medieval lanes
activities.description: Lisbon's oldest neighbourhood: tiled facades, laundry-draped balconies, tiny taverns. Visit the Se Cathedral and Portas do Sol viewpoint.

activities.title: Sunset at Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
activities.location: Our Lady of the Mount Viewpoint
activities.description: Highest viewpoint in the city with sweeping views over the castle, rooftops and the Tagus River. Bring a drink and watch the sunset.

activities.title: Fado dinner in Alfama
activities.description: Live fado (Portugal's soulful folk music) over a traditional dinner at spots like Tasca do Chico or Clube de Fado. Book ahead.

activities.title: Ride Tram 28
activities.description: The iconic yellow tram rattles through Alfama, Graca and Baixa. Board at Martim Moniz early to avoid queues and pickpockets (about 3 EUR on board, cheaper with a Viva Viagem card).

activities.title: Castelo de Sao Jorge
activities.description: Hilltop Moorish castle with ramparts and the best 360-degree views of Lisbon (about 15 EUR). Allow 1.5 hours.

activities.title: Lunch at Time Out Market
activities.description: Huge food hall with stalls from top Portuguese chefs: bacalhau, petiscos, burgers, pasteis de nata and local wine.

activities.title: Chiado and Baixa strolling
activities.description: Browse Livraria Bertrand (the world's oldest bookstore still operating), Rua Augusta, Praca do Comercio and the Santa Justa Lift.

activities.title: Sunset at Miradouro de Santa Catarina
activities.description: Local hangout with live buskers, cheap drinks and river views.

activities.title: Jeronimos Monastery
activities.description: UNESCO-listed masterpiece of Manueline architecture (about 12 EUR, closed Mondays). Go at opening to beat the queue.

activities.title: Belem Tower
activities.description: 16th-century fortress on the river, the symbol of Portugal's Age of Discovery. The view from outside is free; climbing the tower is about 8 EUR.

activities.title: Pasteis de Belem
activities.description: The original custard tart bakery since 1837. Eat them warm with cinnamon and powdered sugar. Line moves fast; eat inside to skip the queue.

activities.title: MAAT and Riverside walk
activities.location: MAAT - Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology
activities.description: Modern art and technology museum with a walkable rooftop. Then stroll the riverfront to the Monument to the Discoveries.

activities.title: Seafood at Cervejaria Ramiro
activities.description: Legendary beer-hall seafood restaurant: tiger prawns, goose barnacles, clams in garlic and the steak sandwich to finish. Arrive early or expect a wait.

activities.title: Train from Rossio to Sintra
activities.description: Trains run every 20 minutes and take about 40 minutes (about 5 EUR return).

activities.title: Pena Palace
activities.description: Colourful Romantic-era palace on a hilltop in a misty forest. Buy timed tickets online; allow 2 hours. Take the 434 bus up from the station.

activities.title: Quinta da Regaleira
activities.description: Mystical estate with an initiation well spiralling underground, secret tunnels and gardens. About 12 EUR. Lunch in Sintra village; try a travesseiro pastry at Piriquita.

activities.title: Train on to Porto
activities.description: Return to Lisbon (Oriente or Santa Apolonia) and take the Alfa Pendular to Porto Campanha (about 3 hours). Arrive and check in at The Yeatman (luxury), Pestana Vintage Porto (heritage, riverside) or Gallery Hostel (budget).

activities.title: Ribeira waterfront walk
activities.description: UNESCO-listed riverside district with pastel houses, cafes and rabelo boats. Cross the lower deck of the Dom Luis I Bridge.

activities.title: Livraria Lello
activities.description: One of the world's most beautiful bookshops with a carved staircase (ticket about 8 EUR, redeemable on a book). Book timed entry online.

activities.title: Lunch at Mercado do Bolhao
activities.description: Renovated historic market with fresh produce, cheese, charcuterie and petiscos.

activities.title: Port cellar tour and tasting in Gaia
activities.description: Cross the bridge to Vila Nova de Gaia. Tour a historic lodge such as Graham's, Taylor's or Calem and taste ruby, tawny and white ports (about 15-25 EUR).

activities.title: Dinner at a Ribeira terrace
activities.description: Grilled sardines, octopus rice or bacalhau with a glass of vinho verde. Sunset from the Gaia side is magical.

activities.title: Sao Bento Station azulejo tiles
activities.description: The station hall is covered in 20,000 hand-painted blue tiles depicting Portuguese history. Free to enter.

activities.title: Clerigos Tower and Church
activities.description: Climb 225 steps for panoramic views over Porto's red rooftops (about 8 EUR).

activities.title: Francesinha at Cafe Santiago
activities.description: Porto's famous sandwich: layered meats and cheese in a spicy tomato-beer sauce. Come hungry.

activities.title: Majestic Cafe and Rua de Santa Catarina
activities.description: Belle Epoque cafe where J.K. Rowling wrote early Harry Potter pages. Browse the pedestrian shopping street.

activities.title: Sunset at Jardim do Morro
activities.description: Gaia viewpoint where locals gather with drinks to watch the sun set over the Douro and the bridge.

activities.title: Scenic train from Sao Bento to Pinhao
activities.description: About 2.5 hours up the Douro line, hugging the river. Sit on the right-hand side for the best views of terraced vineyards. Buy tickets on cp.pt.

activities.title: Wine tasting at a quinta in Pinhao
activities.description: Visit Quinta do Bomfim (Symington Family Estates) or Quinta de la Rosa for a tour and tasting of Douro reds and ports among the vines (about 15-30 EUR).

activities.title: Lunch with a view and Douro river cruise
activities.description: Traditional lunch at a quinta terrace, then a 1-2 hour river cruise through the terraced valley. Return to Porto by train in the late afternoon.

activities.title: Farewell dinner back in Porto
activities.description: End the trip with tripas a moda do Porto or a final bacalhau and a glass of tawny port.

data.description:
A 7-day Portugal classic: two days in hilly, tiled Lisbon, a day among the palaces of Sintra, then north to Porto's riverfront and a wine-country day trip into the Douro Valley. Best months: April to June and September to October (warm, fewer crowds). Budget roughly $110-200 USD per person per day.

GETTING THERE & AROUND: Fly into Lisbon (LIS), 20 min by metro to the centre. Buy a Viva Viagem card for metro, trams and buses. Take the Alfa Pendular or Intercidades train Lisbon to Porto (about 3 hrs, book on cp.pt). Sintra is a 40 min train from Rossio station. Skip a rental car in Lisbon and Porto: parking is painful.

WHERE TO STAY
- Lisbon (nights 1-4): Memmo Alfama (luxury boutique with a rooftop pool and river views), Lisboa Carmo Hotel (mid-range, central, in Chiado), Home Lisbon Hostel (budget, lively, family dinners).
- Porto (nights 5-7): The Yeatman (luxury wine hotel across the river in Vila Nova de Gaia), Pestana Vintage Porto (heritage building right on the Ribeira waterfront), Gallery Hostel (budget, artsy, central).

DAY BY DAY
Day 1: Arrive, check in, explore Alfama on foot. Sunset at Miradouro da Senhora do Monte. Fado dinner.
Day 2: Tram 28 ride, Se Cathedral, Castelo de Sao Jorge, Time Out Market lunch, Chiado and Baixa strolling, sunset drinks at Miradouro de Santa Catarina.
Day 3: Belem: Jeronimos Monastery, Belem Tower, Pasteis de Belem, MAAT museum, riverside walk. Evening seafood at Cervejaria Ramiro.
Day 4: Sintra day trip: Pena Palace, Quinta da Regaleira, Moorish Castle. Then train to Porto in the evening or next morning.
Day 5: Porto Ribeira district, Livraria Lello, Dom Luis I Bridge, Port cellar tour and tasting in Gaia.
Day 6: Sao Bento station tiles, Clerigos Tower, Majestic Cafe, francesinha dinner, sunset at Jardim do Morro.
Day 7: Douro Valley day trip by train to Pinhao: vineyards, quinta wine tasting and a river cruise.

MUST-EATS: Pasteis de nata (Pasteis de Belem is the original), bacalhau (salt cod), grilled sardines, francesinha in Porto, ginjinha cherry liqueur, vinho verde and tawny port.

TIPS: Wear flat grippy shoes: cobbled hills are slippery. Buy Pena Palace and Regaleira tickets online and arrive when they open. Book the Douro train seats ahead on weekends. Many restaurants close Sundays or Mondays. Beware of pickpockets on Tram 28.

data.title: Rome, Florence & Venice, Italy: 7 Days of Art, Ruins & Pasta
data.subtitle: The Colosseum, the Vatican, Renaissance Florence and gondolas in Venice on a high-speed train loop

activities.title: Arrive at Fiumicino and ride the Leonardo Express
activities.description: Take the Leonardo Express (14 EUR, 32 min) to Roma Termini. Address: Piazza dei Cinquecento, 00185 Roma RM. Check in at Hotel Campo de' Fiori (Via del Biscione, 6, 00186 Roma), Hotel Artemide (Via Nazionale, 22, 00184 Roma) or The Yellow Hostel (Via Palestro, 44, 00185 Roma).

activities.title: Trevi Fountain
activities.description: Throw a coin over your shoulder for a return to Rome. Go in the evening when the crowd thins and the fountain is lit. Address: Piazza di Trevi, 00187 Roma RM.

activities.title: Gelato at Giolitti
activities.description: Historic gelateria since 1900 serving classic flavours. Address: Via degli Uffici del Vicario, 40, 00186 Roma RM.

activities.title: Spanish Steps at sunset
activities.description: Climb the 135 steps for views over the rooftops. Address: Piazza di Spagna, 00187 Roma RM.

activities.title: Dinner at Roscioli Salumeria con Cucina
activities.description: Famous deli-restaurant for carbonara, cured meats and an excellent wine list. Book ahead. Address: Via dei Giubbonari, 21, 00186 Roma RM.

activities.title: Colosseum
activities.description: Iconic 80 AD amphitheatre. Book timed tickets online (about 18-24 EUR, combo with Forum and Palatine). Address: Piazza del Colosseo, 1, 00184 Roma RM.

activities.title: Roman Forum and Palatine Hill
activities.description: Wander the ruins of ancient Rome's political centre and the hill where emperors lived. Address: Via della Salara Vecchia, 5/6, 00186 Roma RM.

activities.title: Lunch near Monti
activities.description: Walk 10 min to the Monti neighbourhood for pasta and Aperol spritz at a local trattoria. Address area: Via Urbana, 00184 Roma RM.

activities.title: Capitoline Museums and viewpoint
activities.description: Michelangelo-designed square with ancient sculptures, and a rooftop view over the Forum. Address: Piazza del Campidoglio, 1, 00186 Roma RM.

activities.title: Dinner in Trastevere at Da Enzo al 29
activities.description: Beloved trattoria for cacio e pepe, carbonara and artichokes. Expect a queue. Address: Via dei Vascellari, 29, 00153 Roma RM.

activities.title: Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel
activities.description: World-class art collection ending in Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel (about 20 EUR; book skip-the-line weeks ahead). Allow 3 hours. Address: Viale Vaticano, 00165 Roma RM.

activities.title: St. Peter's Basilica and dome climb
activities.description: Largest church in the world. Free entry; the dome climb is about 10 EUR. Cover shoulders and knees. Address: Piazza San Pietro, 00120 Citta del Vaticano.

activities.title: Pantheon
activities.description: Nearly 2,000-year-old temple with an open oculus. Entry about 5 EUR. Address: Piazza della Rotonda, 00186 Roma RM.

activities.title: Piazza Navona
activities.description: Baroque square with Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers. Address: Piazza Navona, 00186 Roma RM.

activities.title: Aperitivo and dinner at Campo de' Fiori
activities.description: Lively square with a daytime market and nightlife. Address: Campo de' Fiori, 00186 Roma RM.

activities.title: Frecciarossa Rome to Florence
activities.description: Depart Roma Termini (Piazza dei Cinquecento, 00185 Roma) for Firenze Santa Maria Novella (Piazza della Stazione, 50123 Firenze). About 1.5 hours. Drop bags at Hotel Brunelleschi (Piazza Santa Elisabetta, 3, 50122 Firenze), Hotel Davanzati (Via Porta Rossa, 5, 50123 Firenze) or Plus Florence (Via Santa Caterina d'Alessandria, 15, 50129 Firenze).

activities.title: Duomo and Brunelleschi's Dome
activities.location: Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore
activities.description: Climb 463 steps of the dome (reserve a time slot) and view Giotto's Campanile. Address: Piazza del Duomo, 50122 Firenze FI.

activities.title: Lunch at All'Antico Vinaio
activities.description: Legendary sandwich shop with huge schiacciata sandwiches. Address: Via dei Neri, 65r, 50122 Firenze FI.

activities.title: Uffizi Gallery
activities.description: Botticelli's Birth of Venus and works by Leonardo, Michelangelo and Raphael. Book timed tickets (about 25 EUR). Address: Piazzale degli Uffizi, 6, 50122 Firenze FI.

activities.title: Ponte Vecchio at golden hour
activities.description: Medieval bridge lined with goldsmith shops. Address: Ponte Vecchio, 50125 Firenze FI.

activities.title: Accademia Gallery (Michelangelo's David)
activities.description: See the original David (book timed entry, about 16 EUR). Address: Via Ricasoli, 58-60, 50129 Firenze FI.

activities.title: Mercato Centrale
activities.description: Two-floor food hall with Tuscan lampredotto, pasta, pizza and gelato. Address: Piazza del Mercato Centrale, 50123 Firenze FI.

activities.title: Pitti Palace and Boboli Gardens
activities.description: Grand Renaissance palace and sculpted gardens with city views. Address: Piazza de' Pitti, 1, 50125 Firenze FI.

activities.title: Sunset at Piazzale Michelangelo
activities.description: Best panoramic view over Florence; walk up from the river or take bus 12/13. Address: Piazzale Michelangelo, 50125 Firenze FI.

activities.title: Dinner at Trattoria Za Za
activities.description: Tuscan classics like ribollita, pappa al pomodoro and bistecca. Book ahead. Address: Piazza del Mercato Centrale, 26r, 50123 Firenze FI. (For a lunch alternative, Trattoria Mario, Via Rosina, 2r, 50123 Firenze FI, is a classic lunch-only spot.)

activities.title: Frecciarossa Florence to Venice
activities.description: Depart Firenze Santa Maria Novella (Piazza della Stazione, 50123 Firenze) for Venezia Santa Lucia (Fondamenta Santa Lucia, 30121 Venezia). About 2 hours. Hotels: Hotel Danieli (Riva degli Schiavoni, 4196, 30122 Venezia), Hotel Ala (Campo Santa Maria del Giglio, 2494, 30124 Venezia) or Generator Venice (Fondamenta Zitelle, 86, 30133 Venezia).

activities.title: St. Mark's Basilica
activities.description: Golden Byzantine mosaics and the Pala d'Oro altarpiece (about 3 EUR, reserve online). Address: Piazza San Marco, 328, 30124 Venezia VE.

activities.title: Doge's Palace
activities.description: Gothic palace and the Bridge of Sighs. Address: Piazza San Marco, 1, 30124 Venezia VE.

activities.title: Gondola ride
activities.description: Shared or private ride through quiet canals (about 80-100 EUR for 30 min, private). Departs from Bacino Orseolo, near Piazza San Marco, 30124 Venezia.

activities.title: Cicchetti crawl at Cantina Do Mori
activities.description: Tiny wine bar from 1462 for small snacks and an ombra of wine. Address: Calle dei Do Mori, 429, 30125 Venezia VE.

activities.title: Rialto Market
activities.description: Morning fish and produce market beside the Rialto Bridge. Coffee at a nearby cafe. Address: Campo de la Pescaria, 30125 Venezia VE.

activities.title: Gallerie dell'Accademia
activities.description: Venice's finest collection of Venetian painting. Address: Campo della Carita, 1050, 30123 Venezia VE.

activities.title: Vaporetto to Murano glass
activities.description: Take line 4.1 or 4.2 to Murano and visit the Glass Museum. Address: Fondamenta Giustinian, 8, 30141 Venezia VE.

activities.title: Burano colourful houses
activities.description: Ride on to the lace island with painted houses. Address: Piazza Baldassare Galuppi, 30142 Venezia VE.

activities.title: Head to Marco Polo Airport
activities.description: Alilaguna boat or ATVO bus to Venice Marco Polo Airport (VCE). Address: Viale Galileo Galilei, 30, 30173 Tessera, Venezia.

data.description:
A 7-day Italy greatest-hits trip by high-speed train: three days in Rome among ancient ruins and the Vatican, two in Renaissance Florence, and two in Venice's canals and islands. Best months: April to June and September to October. Avoid August (heat and closures). Budget roughly $140-280 USD per person per day.

GETTING THERE & AROUND: Fly into Rome Fiumicino (FCO); the Leonardo Express train reaches Termini in 32 min. Rome to Florence by Frecciarossa is about 1.5 hrs, Florence to Venice about 2 hrs (book at trenitalia.com or italotreno.it; cheapest 2-8 weeks ahead). Rome and Florence's centres are walkable. Venice has no cars: use vaporetto water buses (24-48 hr passes) and your feet.

WHERE TO STAY
- Rome (nights 1-3): Hotel Campo de' Fiori (Via del Biscione 6, rooftop terrace, mid-range), Hotel Artemide (Via Nazionale 22, upscale near Termini), The Yellow Hostel (Via Palestro 44, budget near Termini).
- Florence (nights 4-5): Hotel Brunelleschi (Piazza Santa Elisabetta 3, luxury in a medieval tower beside the Duomo), Hotel Davanzati (Via Porta Rossa 5, mid-range, central), Plus Florence (Via Santa Caterina d'Alessandria 15, budget hostel with a pool).
- Venice (nights 6-7): Hotel Danieli (Riva degli Schiavoni 4196, luxury palace on the lagoon), Hotel Ala (Campo Santa Maria del Giglio 2494, mid-range near San Marco), Generator Venice (Fondamenta Zitelle 86, Giudecca, budget).

DAY BY DAY
Day 1: Arrive in Rome, check in, Trevi Fountain, Spanish Steps and a Roman dinner.
Day 2: Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine Hill, then Trastevere for dinner.
Day 3: Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel and St. Peter's Basilica, then Pantheon and Piazza Navona.
Day 4: Morning train to Florence. Duomo, Uffizi Gallery and Ponte Vecchio.
Day 5: Accademia (Michelangelo's David), Boboli Gardens and sunset at Piazzale Michelangelo.
Day 6: Morning train to Venice. St. Mark's Basilica, Doge's Palace and a gondola ride.
Day 7: Rialto Market, Accademia, island hop to Murano and Burano, then depart.

MUST-EATS: Carbonara, cacio e pepe and supplì in Rome; bistecca alla fiorentina and schiacciata sandwiches in Florence; cicchetti (small bites) and spritz in Venice; gelato daily.

TIPS: Book the Colosseum, Vatican Museums, Uffizi and Accademia timed tickets weeks ahead. Cover shoulders and knees for churches. Validate regional train tickets before boarding. Watch for pickpockets near Termini and tourist sites. Skip restaurants with photo menus on the main squares.

data.title: Cape Town & the Winelands, South Africa: 7 Days of Mountains, Penguins & Wine
data.subtitle: Table Mountain, the Cape Peninsula, Robben Island, Stellenbosch vineyards and whale season in Hermanus

activities.title: Arrive in Cape Town and check in
activities.description: Land at Cape Town International (CPT) and take an Uber or Bolt (about 25 min). Stay at The Silo Hotel (luxury, Waterfront), Daddy Long Legs Hotel (mid-range, Long Street) or Ashanti Lodge (budget, Gardens).

activities.title: V&A Waterfront stroll
activities.description: Working harbour with shops, street performers, seal spotting at the Clock Tower and views of Table Mountain. Visit the Zeitz MOCAA art museum in the Silo District (about 250 ZAR).

activities.title: Sunset and dinner at the Waterfront
activities.description: Try fresh Cape seafood or a braai plate at a harbour-side restaurant such as Harbour House or Willoughby & Co sushi. Book a table at sunset.

activities.title: Table Mountain by cable car or hike
activities.description: Ride the rotating cable car (about 420 ZAR return; buy online and check wind status that morning) or hike Platteklip Gorge (2-3 hrs, steep). Walk the flat top trails and look down on the city and Atlantic.

activities.title: Bo-Kaap and Cape Malay lunch
activities.description: Cobbled streets of bright candy-coloured houses. Visit the Bo-Kaap Museum and eat a Cape Malay curry, samosas and koesisters at Bo-Kaap Kombuis or Biesmiellah.

activities.title: Camps Bay beach and Twelve Apostles views
activities.description: Atlantic seaboard beach strip backed by mountains. The water is cold but the scenery is fantastic.

activities.title: Sundowners on Signal Hill or at Camps Bay
activities.description: Order a Pinotage or a gin and tonic with a view of the sun dropping into the sea.

activities.title: Drive Chapman's Peak (Chappies) toll road
activities.description: One of the world's great coastal drives: 9 km carved into cliffs between Hout Bay and Noordhoek (small toll). Stop at viewpoints.

activities.title: Hout Bay harbour and seal island boat trip
activities.description: Short boat trip to Duiker Island to see hundreds of Cape fur seals. Fish and chips on the quay afterwards.

activities.title: Cape Point and Cape of Good Hope
activities.description: Cape of Good Hope Nature Reserve (about 380 ZAR entry). Ride the Flying Dutchman funicular or hike to the lighthouse and look for baboons, ostriches and bontebok. Take the photo at the Cape of Good Hope sign.

activities.title: Boulders Beach African penguins
activities.description: Walk the boardwalks to see African penguins nesting and swimming. Entry about 190 ZAR. Lunch or sundowners in Simon's Town.

activities.title: Robben Island ferry and tour
activities.description: Ferry from the Nelson Mandela Gateway at the V&A Waterfront (about 3.5 hours total). Tour the prison led by former political prisoners and see Mandela's cell. Book 1-2 weeks ahead.

activities.title: Lunch at the Waterfront or Gardens
activities.description: Light lunch before heading to Kirstenbosch.

activities.title: Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden
activities.description: Spectacular garden on the slopes of Table Mountain, home to rare fynbos. Walk the Boomslang canopy walkway (about 125 ZAR entry). In summer, bring a picnic for the Sunday sunset concerts.

activities.title: Sundowner at Signal Hill
activities.description: Drive up Signal Hill for views over the city lights and Table Bay.

activities.title: Drive to Stellenbosch (about 45 min)
activities.description: Head east on the N2 and R310 to the university town surrounded by vineyards and oak-lined streets. Check in at Delaire Graff (luxury), Oude Werf Hotel (mid-range) or a guesthouse.

activities.title: Estate wine tasting
activities.description: Visit estates such as Spier, Tokara, Delaire Graff or Lanzerac. Taste Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinotage and Chenin Blanc. Budget about 150-300 ZAR per tasting. Always use a designated driver or hire a wine-tour driver.

activities.title: Long lunch among the vines
activities.description: Many estates have terraces with local produce: try Jonkershuis (Spier), Overture (Hidden Valley) or Rust en Vrede. Book ahead on weekends.

activities.title: Walk Stellenbosch town centre
activities.description: Dorp Street has Cape Dutch architecture, galleries, art shops and cafes.

activities.title: Drive to Franschhoek
activities.description: Scenic 30 min drive over the Helshoogte Pass to the French-founded valley, known as the gourmet capital of South Africa.

activities.title: Franschhoek Wine Tram
activities.description: Hop-on hop-off tram and bus linking estates (about 500-800 ZAR). Includes tastings at several wineries with scenic views.

activities.title: Cheese and charcuterie lunch
activities.description: Enjoy local cheese boards, cured meats and olives at a winery terrace or town cafe.

activities.title: Huguenot Memorial and Main Street
activities.description: Learn about the French Huguenot settlers who brought winemaking to the valley. Browse boutiques and chocolatiers.

activities.title: Drive to Hermanus via Sir Lowry's Pass
activities.description: About 1.5 hours along the R44 Clarence Drive or via the N2. Stops for views over False Bay and Betty's Bay.

activities.title: Whale watching from the Cliff Path
activities.description: Southern right whales visit between roughly August and November; Hermanus is called the best land-based whale watching in the world. Walk the 12 km cliff path or take a boat tour. Outside whale season, enjoy shark cage diving in Gansbaai.

activities.title: Seafood lunch on the harbour
activities.location: The Rock Restaurant , New Harbour Hermanus
activities.description: Fresh line-fish, calamari and prawns at Harbour Rock or the Fisherman's Cottage.

activities.title: Drive back to Cape Town for departure
activities.description: About 1.5 to 2 hours back to Cape Town International. Return the rental car and check in for your flight.

data.description:
A 7-day South Africa first-timer trip: Cape Town's mountain-meets-ocean scenery, a full Cape Peninsula day with penguins and the Cape of Good Hope, Robben Island and Kirstenbosch gardens, two relaxed days among the Cape Winelands, and a coastal finish in Hermanus. Best months: November to March (warm, long days) and August to November for southern right whales in Hermanus. Budget roughly $90-220 USD per person per day, and your money goes far here.

GETTING THERE & AROUND: Fly into Cape Town International (CPT), about 25 min from the city. Use Uber/Bolt for the city and at night (cheap and the safest option). Rent a car for days 3, 5, 6 and 7: driving is on the left. Download offline maps and keep valuables out of sight in parked cars.

WHERE TO STAY
- Cape Town (nights 1-4): The Silo Hotel (luxury, in a converted grain silo at the Waterfront), Daddy Long Legs Hotel (quirky mid-range on Long Street), Ashanti Lodge (budget hostel in Gardens, great Table Mountain views).
- Winelands (nights 5-6): Delaire Graff Estate (luxury, spectacular valley views), Oude Werf Hotel (mid-range, SA's oldest inn, in Stellenbosch town), or a guesthouse on a wine estate.
- Night 7: Return to Cape Town or stay in Hermanus at The Marine (luxury) before flying out.

DAY BY DAY
Day 1: Arrive, V&A Waterfront, sunset on the harbour, dinner at the Silo District.
Day 2: Table Mountain by cable car (or hike up Platteklip Gorge), Bo-Kaap's rainbow houses, Camps Bay sunset.
Day 3: Cape Peninsula road trip: Chapman's Peak Drive, Hout Bay, Boulders Beach penguins, Cape Point and the Cape of Good Hope.
Day 4: Robben Island tour in the morning, Kirstenbosch Botanical Garden in the afternoon, sundowner at Signal Hill.
Day 5: Drive to Stellenbosch, estate wine tasting, lunch among the vines, evening in town.
Day 6: Franschhoek wine tram, Huguenot Memorial and cheese and charcuterie lunch.
Day 7: Scenic drive to Hermanus via Sir Lowry's Pass: whales (August-November), cliff path walk and fresh seafood.

MUST-EATS: Braai (barbecue), bunny chow, biltong, boerewors roll, Cape Malay curry in Bo-Kaap, fresh line-fish and calamari, rooibos tea and melktert (milk tart), Pinotage and Chenin Blanc wines.

TIPS: Check Table Mountain cable car status on the day: it closes in high winds. Book Robben Island 1-2 weeks ahead. Tip 10-15% at restaurants. Do not walk around the city centre at night; use rideshare. Carry sunscreen and layers: weather swings quickly. Power sockets are type M/N (bring an adapter).
